tickets.short: Spare hand-added servers from state-driven removal
tickets.long:
The state file lists which servers mcp-sync manages. A server on that list, but no longer in the manifest, gets removed from the live configs. A state file that goes false (a hand edit, a bad merge, cross-machine drift) then deletes a server the user added natively.

The fix: store a fingerprint of each rendered server. Before a removal, compare the live entry to the fingerprint. Spare and unlist an entry that no longer matches, and report the spare.

First step, per the owner at gate C: map the consumers of the managed set before the schema changes. Those are the claude and codex removal paths, save_state, check, and adopt. Defer, but not long. Repro: .map/AGNT-0001/scratch/t19-state/repro/a02.

tickets.short: Merge concurrent applies instead of last-writer-wins
tickets.long:
Two mcp-sync applies against the same target at the same moment each write an intact file, and the later rename wins. The earlier change disappears while both runs report success.

The fix is a conflict pass: after a lost race, re-read the target and merge. Prefer to keep both entries and to maximize compatibility.

Low priority: install.sh invokes the tool one run at a time, and the owner runs one agent at a time. The external-writer guard already refuses blind overwrites. Repro: .map/AGNT-0001/scratch/t19b-concurrency.

Trigger note from the close review: install.sh links itself as the post-merge hook, so a git pull inside a live agent session is the likely real-world path to two concurrent applies.

tickets.short: Rust rag-recall with a relevance gate, registered on Claude and Codex
tickets.long:
The hook injects the top eight chunks on every prompt. Gated retrieval beat that pattern by 2.2 points while it retrieved 70 percent less (TARG). Low-relevance chunks measurably degrade output quality (Chroma context-rot study, 18 models). Stale memories decay into confident wrong answers as the time gap grows.

The fix: inject only when the prompt turns on past work, and otherwise stay silent. The counter-finding sets the bar: a crude keyword gate scored worse than always-on retrieval. The gate must beat that bar, or the hook stays as it is. Anthropic ships the on-demand pattern in its memory tool, which is the fallback shape.

Per the tooling rule, a change to this Python script means a Rust rewrite, never a patch in place. The Codex and Claude registrations both point at the new binary when it lands.

tickets.short: Evaluate the shipped model router, and settle discovery against the static tier file
tickets.long:
RESCOPED 2026-08-20, after a session shipped the thing this ticket said not to build. The original text asked for design only, no runtime code, and model admission through discovered capability, availability, quota, and price rather than a hard-coded list. What landed instead is a working static router: config/model-tiers.json as the one place model ids live, install.sh compiling it into subagents.defaultModel, subagents.agentOverrides and a flat modelTierFallbacks map, tier assignments for 11 agents, a session-level fallback in pi/extensions/usage-limit-continue.ts that walks the tier chain on a usage limit and then resumes on whichever abandoned model returns first, and docs/routing.md as the policy. Treat that as v1 and do not redesign it from scratch.

What remains, in priority order.

1. The evaluation system, which is the half of the original scope nothing has touched. Representative task classes drawn from real dispatches in this repository, fixed inputs, blind grading, repeated trials, uncertainty, model and harness version capture, and content-free result summaries. Two router arms to compare: cheap-first with escalation on a failed check, against predictive tier choice up front.

2. Three findings from the 2026-08-20 session constrain that benchmark, and skipping them repeats the session's mistakes. First, the accept signal cannot be a pass-or-fail gate alone: a free-model run returned the correct answer and still burned 92 seconds, 10 tool calls and 53k tokens, five of them rewriting one file, so a gate-only score keeps it. Count turns and wall-clock beside correctness. Second, the predictive arm must read repository state, not task text: arXiv:2607.00053 reports an information-theoretic error floor for routing agentic work from the task description alone, because a typo and a multi-module refactor read the same. Third, free-tier models failed to terminate cleanly on both observed tool-loop runs, so tool grant shape is a routing variable, not a detail.

3. Do not write the harness from scratch. ulab-uiuc/LLMRouter ships ten router baselines including the cheap-first cascade, lm-sys/RouteLLM scores routers, and FrugalGPT (arXiv:2305.05176) and AutoMix (arXiv:2310.12963) are the published form of the cheap-first arm. Their corpora are one-shot quiz prompts (RouterBench, MMLU, GSM8K, MBPP, MT-Bench) and do not transfer, because the accept signal here is whether a gate passed in this repository. Borrow the method and the metric definitions; write the cases locally.

4. Settle discovery against the static list, on evidence rather than preference. The static file is correct today and the owner's instinct on 2026-08-20 was right that it is hard-coded. The failure it will eventually hit is staleness when a provider ships a model or moves a price, and the cheapest answer is probably a refresh that reconciles config/model-tiers.json against the live registry in ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, not a capability-discovery engine. Decide with a case where the list actually went stale.

5. Still open from the original scope, and still unbuilt: separating model, provider, account and harness so one model is reachable by any allowed route; covering Codex alongside Claude Code and pi; the quota shadow price that makes a subscription-backed call cost something; a cold-start policy for new models; and an exploration budget that cannot overspend. Each needs a worked example before it earns code.

Acceptance: a benchmark that runs both arms over the local corpus and reports cost per accepted artifact with turns and latency, a decision record naming which arm won and on which task classes, and either a registry-refresh path or a written reason the static file stays hand-edited.

Owner's addition, 2026-08-20: the benchmark should also sweep PER ARTIFACT, not only per router. Run an artifact's own eval cases once on each enabled model and report score beside cost and latency, so the tier assignment for each skill and agent comes from measurement instead of judgment. In his words: "its worth to add a run in each model when running evals for our agent artifacts (ai-author) to see which models are acceptable, which tiers are more efficient for each skill/agent/etc". Build it opt-in, as a --sweep flag on the existing harnesses rather than the default run, because every case times nine enabled models is expensive enough that a default would stop anyone running evals at all. The log-summarizer tiering on 2026-08-20 is the worked example: four runs moved it off T1, and a sweep would have answered that in one command.

Owner's refinement, same day: do not run all nine. Walk UP from the cheapest tier and stop at the first one whose output is acceptable, then record that as the artifact's minimum. In his words: "run it from the bottom up and when output is acceptable then we mark that as the minimum". Two guards, both earned on 2026-08-20. First, one run is a sample of one: the free tier passed a log-summary task and failed the identical task on the next run, so a tier is only accepted after repeat trials clear the threshold, never on a single pass. Second, record the FAILING tier directly below the accepted one, because the boundary is the reusable fact, and it is what makes a re-test cheap when a model or a price moves. Watch for non-monotonicity while doing it: a larger model can fail a format-strict case a smaller one passes, so first-pass-going-up equals the true minimum only once the repeats confirm it. Starting rung is a judgment call, and T2 is the sane default, since T1 failed three of four runs and its failures cost 92 and 150 seconds of latency rather than money. This also turns every metadata.minimum-tier floor into a hypothesis: the four authoring skills carry T4 on judgment alone, and this sweep is what can falsify that.

tickets.short: engineer map defect batch from RAG-0001 (files truth, oracle check, counter assert)
tickets.long:
Phase 18's stash content check compares the stashed files against the union of every task's `files` array. On RAG-0001 four files were in the stash that no task claimed: `Cargo.lock`, `.gitignore`, `parity/config.toml` and `src/env_lock.rs`. Two classes of gap produced them. A task that edits `Cargo.toml` generates `Cargo.lock` and never declares it. And a phase-15 fix that CREATES a file never appends it to the owning task, so the file exists with no owner. The check then reads as a possible contaminated stash when it is really an incomplete inventory, which costs a careful reader real time at the one gate where a wrong call is catastrophic. Recorded as D-22. FIX: phase 08 declares generated companions alongside their source, and a phase-15 resolution appends any file it creates to the task it belongs to.

FOLDED IN AGNT-0020 (owner, gate A, 2026-08-20): A break-panel verdict is only as good as the oracle it is measured against, and nothing in phase 19 checks the oracle. On RAG-0001 the terminal harness used `pyte`, which SILENTLY DISCARDS the rest of a line after U+200D. Every bidi and zero-width-joiner verdict it produced was therefore unsound. It generated a finding that survived TWO rounds and consumed a debugging cycle before round 3 replaced the oracle with tmux and got 77 of 77 agreement with the binary - proving the code had been right the whole time. The failure mode is worse than a missed bug, because it manufactures work and can drive a correct implementation into being changed. FIX: before a harness's verdicts are trusted, run it against a case with a known answer and confirm it agrees. Where an angle depends on a third-party emulator or parser, name it and its version in the report.

FOLDED IN AGNT-0021 (owner, gate A, 2026-08-20): `next_nnnn` drifted to one less than it should be on the RAG-0001 run, so the next ticket filed would have collided with an existing id. THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE SKILL: a ticket was filed by hand at gate C, outside phase 22, and phase 22 already states that only its own step may increment the counter. So this ticket is a guard against a rule already being broken, not a missing rule. It is filed anyway because the failure is silent and permanent - a duplicate id cannot be renumbered, since /task-graph refuses renumbering by design - and the check is one line. FIX: assert `next_nnnn == max(NNNN) + 1` on entry to phase 22 and on any roadmap write, and fail loudly.

tickets.short: Auto-continue agents when a usage limit resets (5h/7d)
tickets.long: A Pi extension (pi/extensions/usage-limit-continue.ts) watches after_provider_response for a 429 and message_end for an assistant stopReason="error" whose errorMessage names a usage or rate limit. It resolves a reset instant from response headers (retry-after, *-reset), from reset phrasing in the error text ("resets at", "resets in"), or, failing both, from the 5-hour session window or 7-day weekly window the text names. Local models (ollama/lmstudio/localhost baseUrl) are exempt. On a resolved instant it spawns a detached sleep-then-resume shell job (sleep <wait>, then pi --session <file> --print continue), recorded under ~/.pi/agent/usage-limit-continue/pending.json to avoid a duplicate schedule, and exposes /usage-limit-status. A secondary Rust tool, tools/usage-limit-watch, tails a plain-text log (for headless codex/claude runs whose output is redirected to a file) for the same phrasing and schedules a caller-supplied resume command the same way; it has no access to HTTP headers or model metadata, so a caller passes --local for a log known to be a local model. Both are wired into config/tools.toml and install.sh respectively. Executed directly rather than through the full engineer 23-phase spine, given turn budget; verification: 23 TS unit tests (node --test) and a strict tsc --noEmit pass against both the installed and the latest published @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent types, 7 Rust unit tests plus a real end-to-end run (cargo clippy -D warnings clean), and an install.sh --dry-run/live run against a scratch REPO_TARGET/HOME confirming the new step wires correctly. Not done: an interactive Codex/Claude TUI wrapper (would need PTY passthrough, a materially larger effort) — usage-limit-watch covers only redirected/logged output for those two tools.

tickets.short: ai-author proposes artifacts from mined session evidence
tickets.long: ai-author decides whether to author only once an authoring job arrives: its own opening section routes what arrived, and the tree answers should-this-exist, never should-anyone-have-noticed. Nothing in the system watches accumulated evidence and proposes a capability unprompted. Mine the evidence that already exists: per-artifact logs/usage.jsonl, run-history.jsonl, and the session transcripts indexed in the personal RAG(Retrieval Augmented Generation) store. Look for a task shape repeated across sessions that the runner currently does inline. Propose a skill by default; propose an agent only on the three grounds that justify one, a different model, a tool grant the runner should not hold, or isolation from a job that spews noise. Guards, both required: the standing answer is zero, per docs/agents-fleet-research.md line 94 (handful, real-writeup ceiling ~5, null hypothesis zero), and every proposal carries the cost it measured rather than a plausible improvement idea, or the section becomes a monthly list that bills a day each and saves nothing. Run it on an interval through the pi-subagents scheduler. Owner asked for this on 2026-08-20, in his words: "it would also be in charge of checking my sessions to find recurring tasks or inneficiencies that could be skills, or subagents if they need a specific agent". Ships as a section inside skills/ai-author/SKILL.md plus eval cases, never as a new sibling artifact, because ai-author rule 1 bans authoring a sibling for a capability an existing artifact owns.

tickets.short: subagent runs drop context.md into the repo root
tickets.long: Every pi-subagents dispatch that leaves the output default alone writes its result to context.md in the repository root and reports it as savedOutputPath. Seen four times in one session on 2026-08-20 (runs 5137e1ca, 8a33cc0c, ef5a3b5b, 721e8478), each leaving an untracked file in a working tree. That is the exact shape the engineer map already bans a phase commit from sweeping up, since widening a commit to git add -A is what put ticket artifacts into a product repo history before. One free-model run rewrote the same context.md five times inside a single dispatch, so the file also churns. Fix at the config layer so the artifact never lands in a project repo: set the subagent output default to false, or point it under the run directory. Gitignoring it is the fallback, not the preference, because it hides the litter instead of stopping it.

tickets.short: audit every skill against current research, and measure its cheapest passing tier
tickets.long:
Two halves, one ticket, because neither half is decidable alone: what a skill SAYS and which model is cheap enough to run it are the same question asked twice.

HALF ONE, the tier staircase. docs/routing.md calls every skill floor a hypothesis, and it is right. metadata.minimum-tier sits on 13 skills today and rests on judgment, never on measurement. Run each skill's eval cases at T1, T2, T3 and T4 and report, per skill, the CHEAPEST tier whose score stays inside noise of the best tier. That number replaces the judgment floor.

A blocker comes first, and skipping it makes every staircase number meaningless. The harness in skills/*/evals/run.sh does NOT execute the skill. It sends the SKILL TEXT plus the case plus the rubric to a judge and asks whether an agent following that text WOULD meet EXPECT. That grades prose, not capability, so the same score comes back on every tier. The staircase needs a second arm that RUNS the skill on the candidate tier model against the case input, and then grades the artifact the run produced. Build that arm first. The judge is also hardcoded as `claude -p` in 15 copies of run.sh; the judge model belongs in config/model-tiers.json, and it must sit at a fixed tier ABOVE the arm under test so no model grades itself.

Score each (skill, tier) cell on more than pass-or-fail. AGNT-0018 recorded a free model that answered correctly and still burned 92 seconds, 10 tool calls and 53k tokens, five calls rewriting one file. A gate-only score keeps that model. Count turns, wall clock, tokens and cost beside correctness, repeat each cell, and report the spread. AGNT-0018 needs the same execution arm for its router arms; whichever ticket starts first builds it, and neither blocks the other.

HALF TWO, the content audit. Sweep the current literature on skill and prompt authoring, and re-read every skill against what survives the sweep. ai-author is audited by the same pass and gets no exemption, together with skill-author, agent-author and workflow-author, because a defect in an authoring skill is copied into every artifact it writes. GEPA(Genetic-Pareto prompt evolution) is the loop ai-author already runs; find what has superseded or corrected it since. A finding lands only through the GEPA loop's own accept rule: a change ships when the holdout score moves outside noise, never on taste, and a defect fix ships on a reproduction plus a case authored in the same pass.

THE POLICY GAP the owner named on 2026-08-20, and the reason he asked for this ticket. minimum-tier is a FLOOR and nothing else. No mechanism routes a mechanical skill DOWN. create-pr is the example he raised: it carries no floor, so it runs on whatever the session runs, though its whole job is commit, push, gh pr create, plus two grep verifies for attribution lines. Decide the downward path and ship it: either a declared target tier that dispatches the skill body into a cheap child, or a written rule that the runner delegates it. Whatever ships keeps every human gate and both attribution verifies with the parent, because a cheap child must never hold the gate.

FIVE SKILLS SHIP NO CASES: agent-author, agent-config-reset, skill-author, workflow-author and pr-review-filter have no evals/cases.jsonl. They cannot enter the staircase, and the authoring contract already requires the directory, so this pass closes that gap. Four of the five are authoring skills, which is the worst place for the gap to sit.

Owner's ask, in his words on 2026-08-20: "audit all the skills with ai-author and ai-author itself based on newest best practices in academia and research and also run the evals against the tier staircase to find the most usage-efficient method of doing the skills".

tickets.short: phase 07 must probe a surface before writing a contract against it
tickets.long: Four separate defects in the AGNT-0015 run share one cause: contracts written from reading type declarations, without ever executing the surface they describe. D-05, ExtensionContext.exec has no env passthrough, so the engine could not inject GIT_INDEX_FILE. D-08, Pi's require-based loader could not resolve a relative import through a symlink that Node's ESM import resolved fine, which broke extension loading in every Pi session until it was caught. D-13, pi-tui's Box is not importable from this repo at all, so the contract named a dependency that would have thrown at load. And INV-015 was applied to the shell boundary but not to nvim's command line, which is where the injection actually lived. Phase 07 should require one executed probe per external surface a contract names, with the probe's output recorded, before the contract is written.

tickets.short: phase 16's stash check must name the ticket run dir, not all of .map
tickets.long: AGNT-0015 deviation D-09: phase 16's check reads 'the stash names no .map/ path', but the repo-level map files (roadmap.json, invariants.md, inspiration.md, ideation/) are tracked on purpose and are legitimately part of a change, so the check fires on a correct state. It should read '.map/<TICKET-ID>/' — the gitignored run dir is the thing that must never be stashed. One line of wording; the current text teaches the reader to wave a real check through.

tickets.short: every fix must ship a repo test, or it can vanish silently
tickets.long: AGNT-0015 failure F-08: two verified fixes (bidi stripping and row dedup) were lost before ever reaching a commit, and the suite stayed green throughout because both had been proven only by scratch probes, never encoded as repo tests. git log -S showed the code had never existed in any commit. The break panel found the regression rounds later. The engineer map should require that every fix ship a test inside the repo suite — which is exactly what task T15 had to enforce by hand on this run — so that losing the fix turns the suite red.

tickets.short: gate C needs rendered visual evidence before it is presented
tickets.long: On AGNT-0015 the owner found five defects that four full break-panel rounds missed: the selection highlight was invisible, chat text bled through the panel edges, one key was advertised for two jobs, an empty column trapped the user with no way out, and the list had no viewport so anything past the panel height was unreachable. Every one is about what the surface looks like and feels like; none is computable from the code, which is why testers driving the renderer as a function proved it correct while it was unusable. The map should require a rendered artifact — a captured frame or screenshot — as part of preparing gate C, so those defects reach the human before the gate rather than after it.

tickets.short: tool-sync's apply and check disagree about Pi agent destinations
tickets.long: tool-sync --check fails with 'Pi agent destination ~/.pi/agent/agents/anchor-verifier.md collides with a non-symlink', but those files are precisely what tool-sync's own apply step renders: 'render Pi agent <repo>/agents/X/X.md -> ~/.pi/agent/agents/X.md'. Rendering writes a real file; the check demands a symlink. Confirmed not caused by AGNT-0015 — the same failure reproduces with the pre-ticket manifest from commit e2e9de6. The consequence is worse than the bug: any run whose verification includes a tool-sync check now reports a red it cannot fix, which teaches everyone to ignore that check.

tickets.short: a ticket's todo.sh goes stale as walk-backs add tasks
tickets.long: AGNT-0015's todo.sh step1 was written in phase 12 against three test files and never updated when later walk-backs added nvim.test.ts and watch.test.ts, so the ticket's own verification command silently ran 118 of its 138 tests and reported success. Nothing in the map re-checks that todo.sh still matches the task list. Phase 18's exit gate should assert that every test file owned by a task appears in the verification steps, so the script cannot drift away from the work it is supposed to verify.

tickets.short: standalone diff TUI in its own herdr pane, harness-independent
tickets.long: A standalone terminal UI for the live diff, run in its own herdr pane beside the agent - the owner's shape is a terminal at the bottom and the diff at the top - rather than an overlay inside one agent. WHY IT BEATS THE EXTENSION: this repo runs Claude Code, Codex and Pi, and a Pi extension can only ever serve Pi. A standalone process serves all three, and it sidesteps every constraint that cost this ticket time: no keybinding to steal (Pi already binds ctrl+ a b c d g l n o p r s t u v x z, and the rest are standard readline keys), no bracketed-paste behaviour to work around, no stale-context hazard of the AGNT-0028 class, no overlay taking focus, and no coupling to one harness's lifecycle. CENTRAL DESIGN QUESTION, to be answered before building: a standalone process does not know when an agent TURN starts, and the turn counter is what makes the current badge agent-aware. Three candidate answers, all with costs: the Pi extension (and later equivalents for Claude Code and Codex) writes turn markers to a file the TUI reads, which keeps turn-awareness but re-introduces per-harness coupling; the TUI infers turns from write quiescence, which needs no coupling but guesses; or it drops the turn column and shows only the branch basket, which is honest and simplest and loses a feature the owner has been using. SCOPE: Rust per this repo's tooling rule, which means re-implementing the engine that AGNT-0015 built in TypeScript - snapshot via a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE plus write-tree, branch-point baseline through merge-base, committed and uncommitted merged into one origin-tagged basket, per-file patch parsing - plus a ratatui front end for the list and the read-only viewer, and a filesystem watcher. AGNT-0015's contracts, test cases and break-panel findings are the specification: reuse them rather than rediscovering the bidi class rule, the display-width clipping, the nested .git ignore rule, the temp-dir sweep and the rest. RELATIONSHIP TO AGNT-0015: that ticket ships and stays. This one does not replace it until it is at least as good; if it proves out, retiring the extension is a later decision, not a precondition. Related: AGNT-0014 owns the two-tab herdr layout this pane joins, and AGNT-0029 the workspace palette.

tickets.short: gate E lands through a PR when the project has a remote
tickets.long: The engineer skill's phase 23 records the owner's default from 2026-08-07 as a local squash merge into main. He revised it on 2026-08-20: "gate e will run through PR as is the new standard for git projects with a remote". Update skills/engineer/phases/23-close.md so the PR route is the default whenever a remote exists, and the local squash merge remains the route only for a repo with no remote - including the consequence phase 01 already documents, that a squash merge is invisible to its merged-branch sweep and so the ticket must be flipped to done at close, whereas the PR route leaves that flip to the next run's phase 01 after the merge. RESOLVED on the AGNT-0015 branch: the owner asked for the change to be propagated during that run rather than deferred, so SKILL.md, phase 01 and phase 23 all carry the remote-decides-the-route rule and TUNING.md records the reversal.

tickets.short: the expanded diff should word wrap instead of clipping long lines
tickets.long: In the live-diff read-only viewer (pi/extensions/live-diff/overlay.ts, renderViewer and viewerBodyLines), a diff line longer than the frame's interior is CLIPPED, so the tail of a long line is unreadable and there is no horizontal scroll to reach it. It should wrap onto continuation rows instead. Constraints the current code already holds and must keep: every emitted row measures EXACTLY the requested width in display columns, East Asian wide characters count two, no span carries ANSI, and the left and right rails stay aligned. A wrapped continuation row needs a gutter treatment that does not read as a new source line - the line-number gutter should be blank on continuations, not repeated. Decide and record whether wrapping is always on or a toggle, and whether it breaks at a word boundary or at the column; a hard column break is simpler and never hides a character, a word break reads better for prose but can leave a ragged right edge in code.

tickets.short: the viewer's hint says esc closes it, but only q works
tickets.long: The read-only viewer's bottom border advertises "esc back" and Esc does nothing; q is what actually returns to the list. The hint lies, which is the same defect class as the earlier TAB hint that advertised one key for two jobs. This CONFIRMS a question left open during the AGNT-0015 run: mapKey does map the bare Esc byte to close, and the reducer does step back one level, so the byte is not reaching the component. Pi's ui.custom factory hands the extension a KeybindingsManager that the code ignores, and Pi very likely binds Escape at the app level to dismiss an overlay, consuming it first. Fix means one of: claim Escape through the keybindings manager the factory already provides, or accept that Pi owns Escape and correct the hint to name q. Whichever is chosen, the hint must state what is actually bound - a hint that names an unbound key is worse than no hint.

tickets.short: live-diff: a dropped refresh is never re-run, so the badge can stay stale
tickets.long: Static review of the AGNT-0015 branch, live-diff.ts around the isRefreshing latch and the settle handler: a refresh that arrives while another is in flight sets a dirty flag and returns, but nothing re-runs it when the in-flight one finishes. The next EVENT consumes the flag, so on a turn whose last write collides with the settle refresh the badge can hold a stale count until the user does something else. Fix: when a refresh finishes and the dirty flag is set, run one more pass, guarded so it cannot loop.

tickets.short: live-diff: the origin merge takes the wrong kind for a file changed on both sides
tickets.long: Static review, engine.ts in the branchStats merge: when a path appears on both the committed and the uncommitted side, the merged row takes the UNCOMMITTED side's kind. A file ADDED on the branch and then edited in the worktree therefore reports 'modified' against a branch point where it does not exist, and a committed rename that is edited afterwards stops rendering as a rename. Fix: the kind must describe the whole span from the branch point to the worktree - added wins over modified, and a rename on either side survives - and the row should keep renamedFrom from whichever side carries it.

tickets.short: live-diff: overlay height is sampled once and can exceed the frame
tickets.long: Two related findings from the static review of live-diff.ts. First, OVERLAY_MIN_HEIGHT can raise the content budget above the frame's own maxHeight, so on a short terminal the component emits more rows than the frame will hold. Second, the viewer's height budget is read once when the overlay opens, so resizing the terminal while it is open leaves the rendered row count and overlayOptions.maxHeight disagreeing until it is reopened. Fix: clamp the budget to the frame's maximum, and re-read the terminal size per render rather than at open.

tickets.short: live-diff: the temp sweep scans a shared tmpdir on every tree write
tickets.long: Static review, engine.ts sweepStaleTempDirs: the sweep runs on every worktree tree write, which is two to three times per refresh, and each run reads the whole shared temp directory and removes any live-diff-index-* directory older than the cutoff regardless of which process owns it. On a busy machine that is a directory scan per refresh, and two agents sharing a tmpdir can in principle remove each other's directories once one is older than the age guard. Fix: sweep at most once per session or on a timer rather than per write, and scope removal to this process's own prefix.

tickets.short: live-diff: prune comments to the whitelist and drop private-function docstrings
tickets.long: The static review audited the AGNT-0015 diff against docs/comment-style.md and found comments matching none of the five whitelisted shapes. Seven full docstrings sit on MODULE-PRIVATE functions in overlay.ts (viewerLineCount, reduceViewer, windowBody, railed, viewerBorderRow, fitHintItems, renderViewer), and the whitelist admits a docstring only on a declaration used from outside its module; two of those also explain the body. Several comments narrate the line below them and should become an extracted, named helper instead - isColumnScopedKey for the empty-column guard, hintFitsBeside for the header gap branch, padToBodyHeight for the frame filler. Three are war stories that belong in the commit trail, including one about a corrupted source file. One genuine cross-component contract about herdr's bracketed-paste behaviour sits in nvim.test.ts and belongs beside the send-keys loop in nvim.ts, where a reader of that file will actually see it. Test files carry roughly thirty comments that restate the assertion below them; those fold into the test name or the assertion message. RESOLVED on the AGNT-0015 branch rather than deferred, on the owner's instruction: the prune was meant as a task in this run, not a follow-up. Seven private-function docstrings deleted, the unused VIEWER_PAGE_SIZE constant and its docstring deleted, four narration comments replaced by named code (isColumnScopedKey/reduceColumnScoped, hintGapBeside, padToBodyHeight) which also removed three now-unreachable branches, three war stories deleted, the herdr bracketed-paste contract moved from nvim.test.ts to nvim.ts beside the send-keys loop, BodyLine.modelRowIndex renamed selectableRowIndex so the field needs no docstring, and roughly forty assertion-restating comments removed from the two test files. Every remaining docstring in the diff sits on an exported declaration; the four surviving line comments are all contracts with something outside their file.

tickets.short: live-diff tests: share one git fixture instead of a repo per test
tickets.long: The 138-test suite takes 21 seconds, and effectively all of it is in the two files that touch real git: live-diff.test.ts at 21.4s and engine.test.ts at 5.3s standalone. The three pure files finish in under a second together. Each test builds its own temp repository with git init plus commits, so it pays several process spawns before it asserts anything. Testing against real git was a deliberate choice and it caught the index-corruption bug, so the fix is NOT to mock git: it is to build a small number of shared read-only fixture repositories once per file and let tests that only READ from them share one, keeping a private repo only for tests that write. Care needed - the engine writes trees via a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, so a shared fixture must be proven not to mutate.

tickets.short: live-diff: emoji presentation selectors are measured one column short
tickets.long: Found by the second static review of AGNT-0015. overlay.ts derives display width from East Asian Width, which is a PER-CODEPOINT property, and that is structurally blind to presentation selectors. U+FE0F (variation selector 16) has General_Category Mn, so ZERO_WIDTH matches it and charWidth returns 0, and sanitize does not strip it because DISPLAY_UNSAFE covers Cc, Cf, Zl and Zp only. So a text-presentation base that goes wide ONLY under VS16 measures 1 while the terminal draws 2: heart U+2764, sun U+2600, airplane U+2708, warning U+26A0, ballot U+2611, copyright U+00A9, trade mark U+2122, and every keycap such as 1 U+0031 U+FE0F U+20E3. That is an UNDER-count, which is exactly the row-bleeds-past-the-panel-edge defect the generated table was meant to end, on characters that appear routinely in README and markdown hunk lines. Fix means measuring GRAPHEME CLUSTERS rather than codepoints: Intl.Segmenter with granularity grapheme is in Node and would give the cluster boundaries, and a cluster containing U+FE0F measures 2 while the same base with U+FE0E measures 1. Zero width joiner sequences work by accident today - U+200D is Cf so sanitize deletes it and the sequence degrades into separate wide emoji that measure and draw the same - but a grapheme-based measure would handle them properly rather than by luck. Note also that the module's own chrome is East Asian Width Ambiguous and counted 1: the rails, the rounded corners, the horizontal rule, the selected-row gutter U+258C, the fold markers, the middle dot, the arrows and the minus sign U+2212. One column in a western terminal, two in a CJK-configured one. Counting them 1 is the right default but it is currently implicit, and the ticket should make it a stated decision with a test.

tickets.short: live-diff: settle whether nvim accepts a bracketed paste on the command line
tickets.long: The comment at nvim.ts around the send-keys loop states that herdr's send-text and pane run deliver through bracketed paste and that nvim inserts a bracketed paste into the BUFFER whatever mode it is in, and concludes that the command line must therefore be TYPED with send-keys. The static reviewer noticed the premise defeats the conclusion: if it were true whatever the mode, the send-text that follows would put the PATH in the buffer too and the whole sequence could not work. The code demonstrably does work, so the real rule is narrower - most likely that nvim routes a bracketed paste to the cmdline while cmdline mode is active, which is the negation of the stated premise. One of the comment and the code is wrong and a maintainer reading it will fix the wrong one. Settle it by experiment against a real nvim: open a pane, enter cmdline mode with send-keys, send-text a path, and observe where the text lands; then repeat in normal mode and in insert mode. Rewrite the comment to state the rule that actually holds. This matters beyond tidiness because the current shape was adopted after a paste corrupted a real source file, so the next person to touch it needs the true rule, not a plausible one.

tickets.short: live-diff: the nvim filename escaping added by the fix pass is untested
tickets.long: The AGNT-0015 fix pass widened openInNvim's escape class to vim's fnameescape territory and replaced the LF/CR/TAB refusal with a full control-character class, closing a hole where a backtick in a repository filename would run a shell command through vim's backtick expansion. The static reviewer confirmed the new class is correct by reading it, and then found that nvim.test.ts still exercises only space, percent, hash and pipe - the four characters the OLD class already handled. Every character the fix ADDED is unverified by the suite: backtick, asterisk, question mark, dollar, brace, bracket, tilde, angle brackets, ampersand, semicolon, quote characters, and the control-byte refusal including ESC. Add cases for each, asserting on the exact string handed to send-text, plus a refusal case per control byte class (C0, DEL, C1) asserting that openInNvim returns false AND that nothing was sent. Note the reviewer also found the leading plus-or-minus escape is dead code, because the argument is always an absolute path from containedAbsolutePath and so always starts with a slash: either delete it or state why it stays.

tickets.short: live-diff: BodyLine should encode filler rows in its type, not a nullable field
tickets.long: The AGNT-0047 comment prune deleted the docstring on BodyLine.modelRowIndex and renamed the field selectableRowIndex. The reviewer's judgement is that the rename carries what the field IS but not what NULL means, and no rename can carry a nullable field's null case: a reader still has to go to buildBody to learn that null marks a hunk line or a truncation line rather than a selectable row. The restructure the deleted docstring was really asking for is a discriminated union - a row line carrying its index and a filler line carrying none - which makes the null case unrepresentable and needs no comment at all. Small, purely internal, and it removes the last place in the module where a comment was doing a type's job.

tickets.short: snapshot engine for non-git directories and gitignored files
tickets.long: Two of the owner's asks share one subsystem, so they ship as one ticket. First, a directory that is not a git repository must still show what changed during the session's uptime, background changes included. Second, gitignored files must appear at the bottom of the diff list, greyed out but still accessible, and their changes must be noticed. Git can answer neither: an ignored file has no baseline in any tree, and a non-repo has no tree at all. Needs a path-to-hash or mtime snapshot taken at session start, a comparison later, and an honest cost story for large trees. CENTRAL RISK, not an afterthought: making ignored changes visible deliberately reverses the watcher's ignore rule in pi/extensions/live-diff/watch.ts, and that rule exists because node_modules churn would otherwise turn the badge into a git treadmill. The ticket must show the treadmill does not return. (Filed as AGNT-0030 on the AGNT-0015 branch and renumbered to AGNT-0053 when that branch merged: a concurrent session on main had already published a different AGNT-0030. Two sessions took the same next id 51 seconds apart, which is the collision AGNT-0021 predicted.)

tickets.short: drill into a branch's commits from the diff view
tickets.long: The owner's second git scenario: from the diff basket, drill down into the individual commits behind the committed rows. A commit list for the current branch with an expandable diff per commit, reachable from the existing read-only viewer. Overlaps AGNT-0017 (restore a Herdr worktree as a replayable cockpit), which also wants browsable per-request history, so the two should be designed together rather than solving the same navigation twice. (Filed as AGNT-0031 on the AGNT-0015 branch and renumbered to AGNT-0054 when that branch merged: a concurrent session on main had already published a different AGNT-0031. Two sessions took the same next id 51 seconds apart, which is the collision AGNT-0021 predicted.)

tickets.short: enforce a subagent's dispatch scope mechanically
tickets.long: AGNT-0015 deviation D-12: a builder appended a joke comment to .gitignore, a file outside the list its dispatch named, and the orchestrator caught it only because it happened to read git status before committing. Nothing enforced the scope the dispatch stated. Add a mechanical check comparing the files a child actually touched against the file list it was given, and fail or report the difference. Cheap, and it removes a whole class of silent damage. (Filed as AGNT-0032 on the AGNT-0015 branch and renumbered to AGNT-0055 when that branch merged: a concurrent session on main had already published a different AGNT-0032. Two sessions took the same next id 51 seconds apart, which is the collision AGNT-0021 predicted.)

tickets.short: phase 23 should land through /git-sync instead of reimplementing it
tickets.long:
Two skills own landing and they have already drifted. skills/engineer/phases/23-close.md step 7 carries its own route choice, its own push, and its own PR call, while skills/git-sync/SKILL.md owns exactly that job for the whole machine. When the gate E standard changed on 2026-08-20 - a project WITH a remote lands through a PR, a project without lands by local squash merge - the change was propagated by hand into SKILL.md, phase 01 and phase 23, and git-sync was missed. It still carries the old local-squash default. That is the duplication reporting itself.

Fix has two halves. First, update git-sync to the current standard so the skill that owns landing states it correctly. Second, make phase 23 step 7 DELEGATE: it should hand the branch to /git-sync and record what came back, keeping only what is genuinely engineer's - the gate E presentation, the status flips in roadmap.json and tasks.json, and the usage log line. The route choice, the push, the PR body and the branch cleanup all belong to git-sync.

Two constraints learned on the AGNT-0015 run. A squash merge is invisible to git branch --merged, because the squashed commit is new and the branch tip never becomes an ancestor, so whichever skill owns the close-out sweep needs the tree-parity fallback that phase 01 already documents. And create-pr does not gate on its own - it stops only on an empty diff or a rejected push - so the human gate has to stay on engineer's side of the handoff, before the call, never inside it.

tickets.short: / to filter the /diff view
tickets.long: The /diff view has no way to filter down a large changeset. Owner feedback (2026-08-21): took too long to find the change wanted on one step, scanning a long diff manually. Add a '/' keybinding in the /diff view (live-diff overlay) that opens a filter/search input over the visible files or hunks, narrowing the view to matches as the user types.

tickets.short: Show gitignored files in the /diff view when they were edited
tickets.long: The /diff view (live-diff) only shows tracked-file changes. A gitignored file that gets edited during a session (e.g. a generated config, a local override, an untracked scratch file the agent wrote to) never shows up, so the owner can't review it there even though it changed. Owner feedback (2026-08-21): 'i want to see the ignored files in the diff menu if they were edited too.' Add ignored-but-edited files to the /diff view's file list, distinguishable from tracked changes (e.g. an [ignored] tag), sourced by diffing against the file's state at session start rather than against git (git ignores them entirely).

tickets.short: Stop burning weekly Codex Spark quota on subagent dispatches
tickets.long: Owner report (2026-08-21, mid-AGNT-0028 phase 19 break-panel): 'codex spark model needs to be used sparingly. I just realized i basically used up all my weekly usage in a few runs.' During this one ticket's break-panel phase, 8 spec-tester dispatches ran, several defaulting to openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex-spark, and at least one hit 'Codex error: The usage limit has been reached' mid-run and silently fell back to anthropic/claude-sonnet-5. A handful of fresh-context subagent dispatches (research, testing, verification -- the normal cost of this engineering map) exhausted a whole week's Spark allowance. Router changes needed: config/model-tiers.json / docs/routing.md currently route some subagent roles to Spark by default; either move those roles off Spark to a tier with headroom, add a usage-aware fallback that never silently burns the last of a weekly quota, or budget-gate Spark-tier dispatches so a single ticket's fan-out can't exhaust the week. Investigate actual routing.md + model-tiers.json for which tiers/roles currently resolve to Spark and why.

tickets.short: telemetry.ts crashes on the same stale-ctx pattern AGNT-0028 fixed in statusline.ts
tickets.long: Found by AGNT-0028's phase-19 break-panel regression-sweep (2026-08-21), reproduced live: pi/extensions/telemetry.ts's registerLifecycle (lines ~1263-1321) captures ctx.ui into a module-closure statusTarget at session_start/agent_start/agent_settled/session_shutdown, then reuses it unguarded inside pi.events.on('subagent:async-started'|'subagent:async-complete'|'subagent:foreground-complete') handlers, which receive no ctx at all. When the captured ctx.ui goes stale (session replacement, same root cause as AGNT-0028), syncTelemetryStatus (telemetry.ts:1065) throws uncaught -- the exact crash-into-TUI failure mode AGNT-0028 just fixed in statusline.ts, now confirmed present in a sibling extension. Repro: a throwaway bun script driving telemetry.ts's session_start handler with a ctx whose ui getter throws after invalidation; reproduces every time. Fix per the same pattern as AGNT-0028: an isCtxActive-style guard (or reuse a shared helper) before any use of the captured statusTarget. tickets.short: statusline usage cache does not bust on same-provider account switch
tickets.long: Found by AGNT-0028's phase-19 break-panel auth-permissions angle (2026-08-21). pi/extensions/statusline.ts's usageByProvider Map is keyed by provider name only ('anthropic'/'openai-codex'), not by account/token identity. Switching accounts within the same provider (logout/login, or a different token under the same provider string) does not invalidate the cached usage bar -- the old account's percentage keeps rendering until the next successful fetch clears the MIN_FETCH_INTERVAL_MS throttle (up to 60s later). Same pattern applies when a fetch fails due to a malformed/expired token or an auth-backend error: the prior bar is deliberately kept (existing documented behavior, 'a fetch failure keeps the previous bar; the next poll retries'), which also means a wrong-account bar can persist through an auth failure. This is pre-existing design, unchanged by AGNT-0028's stale-ctx fix, and was called out but ruled out of scope in AGNT-0028's research.md/test-cases.md. Open question for triage: is showing briefly-stale same-provider usage acceptable (current behavior, low severity, self-corrects within 60s), or does it warrant keying the cache by an account identifier too. Repro: .map/AGNT-0028/scratch/security/pi/extensions/statusline.test.ts (cases A-01, A-04, A-05).

tickets.short: Pi lacks Claude-Code-style live takeover of a running subagent session
tickets.long: Owner ask (2026-08-21): can he hop into a subagent session in Pi the intimate way he can in Claude Code, rather than just watching it. Confirmed capability, straight from the actually-installed skills/pi-subagents/references/*.md docs (not vendor claims, not web search -- an earlier web_search attempt on this same question returned fabricated results, see AGNT-0062): today's real surface is read-only transcript viewing (/subagents-fleet live fleet inspector, subagent status view:'transcript') plus steer (queue an acknowledged nudge message the child sees at its next safe point). The docs are explicit that even the optional Herdr raw inspector dashboard 'mirrors artifacts rather than attaching to the headless child.' No mode lets the parent actually drive a child's turn interactively -- type into its context, redirect it mid-tool-call the way Claude Code's subagent view allows. Investigate whether this is a pi-subagents package limitation (worth a feature request upstream) or a Pi core constraint (headless child processes may not expose an interactive stdin path at all). If upstream, file/track there; if core, this ticket names the gap for whoever owns closing it. Owner lead (same session): github.com/tintinweb/pi-subagents is a candidate. Its README advertises a conversation viewer -- a live-scrolling overlay of an agent's full conversation, auto-following new content -- plus inline steering: press Enter to open a composer, type, press Enter again, and the message appears as a user message that redirects the agent after its current tool. This is closer to live interactive takeover than the currently-installed nicobailon/pi-subagents (read-only transcript plus an out-of-band acknowledged steer). Not yet confirmed hands-on; evaluate it directly against this ticket's gap before treating it as the answer.

tickets.short: Split install.sh --test into build/build_run/run scripts, non-interactive by default
tickets.long: Owner ask (2026-08-21). install.sh --test pins HOME_TARGET to .install-test-home (a sandbox home inside the worktree) and, per its final step (install.sh:573-581), execs  at the end -- an interactive pi session that blocks the script from returning until the user exits it. That makes every --test run pay for launching and using an interactive pi session even when the goal is just verifying the install steps ran correctly (symlinks, config writes, hook registration, etc.), which slows down incremental install.sh development where the loop is edit-run-check-repeat many times per session. Fix direction per the owner: make --test finish in the background without starting the interactive pi session by default -- keep the sandbox-home construction and all prior steps (1-17) exactly as they are, but make step 18's  opt-in (a separate flag, e.g. --test --interactive, or a second explicit step run only when asked) rather than the automatic default tail of --test. The auth-symlink borrowing logic (real credential linked, never copied) stays as-is regardless of whether the interactive drop happens. Owner follow-up (same session): this non-interactive --test run should also be wired into the branch-checkout flow -- run automatically from hooks/post-checkout (already linked by install.sh:213, already the hook that carries live-checkout work into fresh worktrees) in the background, non-interactively, so an incremental install-script check happens on every branch checkout without the developer remembering to run --test by hand or waiting on it in the foreground. Scope both halves as one ticket: (1) make --test's tail non-interactive by default (no automatic exec into pi), (2) have hooks/post-checkout invoke that non-interactive --test path in the background (backgrounded/detached, not blocking the checkout itself) so incremental builds surface install-script breakage automatically per checkout. Owner design direction (same session): don't jam this into the existing --test flag by adding another mode -- split the concern into separate scripts instead. Something like: a `build` script that runs the install steps (1-17: symlinks, config writes, hook registration, sandbox-home construction) with no pi launch at all; a `run` script that does only the interactive `exec env HOME=... pi` drop (today's step 18), callable standalone once a sandbox home already exists; a `build_run` script that chains build then run, for the case someone explicitly wants today's full --test behavior in one call. hooks/post-checkout (see above) then calls `build` alone, backgrounded, non-interactive -- never `build_run`. Whoever picks this up should propose the exact script boundaries and naming at phase 06/07 rather than treating this description as final; the shape here is the owner's first pass, not a locked spec.

tickets.short: No usage bar ever renders for the openai-codex provider
tickets.long: Owner report (2026-08-21), surfaced during AGNT-0028's gate C re-check: the statusline usage bar never appears when the active model provider is openai-codex (GPT/Codex). Needs live diagnosis (which of the three is actually failing) before a fix -- add temporary logging or a debug flag to distinguish them, reproduce against a real openai-codex session, then fix the actual failure point.

tickets.short: A non-staleness setStatus error still crashes the TUI
tickets.long: Found by AGNT-0028's phase-23 fresh code-reviewer dispatch (2026-08-21), proven with a live repro, not self-reported: a genuine error thrown from ctx.ui.setStatus inside pi/extensions/statusline.ts's render() still escapes as an unhandled rejection carrying a raw stack trace -- the exact TUI-crash shape AGNT-0028 set out to close, reachable through a different trigger. Root cause: session_start/model_select/agent_settled call `void refresh(ctx)` fire-and-forget, which detaches the returned promise from the runner's own try/catch around event emission. AGNT-0028's isCtxActive guard only catches staleness; any OTHER error inside the render/refresh call chain (a genuine UI fault, not session replacement) still propagates uncaught. Pre-existing, not introduced by AGNT-0028's diff -- the fire-and-forget pattern predates that ticket. Fix direction: wrap the body of refresh() (or its call sites) in a top-level try/catch that logs and swallows any non-staleness error too, matching the same absence-UX goal AGNT-0028 established (nothing crashes into the TUI, regardless of cause).

tickets.short: statusline test suite has coverage gaps: unguarded mocks, a tautological case, redundant guards
tickets.long: Found by AGNT-0028's phase-23 fresh code-reviewer dispatch (2026-08-21), each proven with a mutation test, not self-reported. (1) Both pi/extensions/statusline.test.ts and statusline.integration.test.ts expose ctx.ui as a plain non-throwing property, while the real ExtensionContext.ui is an assertActive-guarded getter -- neither test file can detect a stale-ctx crash reached through ctx.ui, one of the two crash sites the ticket names. (2) statusline.test.ts's installFakeSetInterval/installMockFetch restores are not wrapped in try/finally (unlike the integration test, which does this correctly) -- an assertion failure between patch and restore leaves globalThis.setInterval and globalThis.fetch permanently replaced for the rest of the test process. (3) render()'s guard (line ~221) and refresh()'s post-fetch guard (line ~249) are mutually redundant and only jointly load-bearing -- deleting either one alone leaves all 7 tests green, so a future cleanup that removes one is unopposed by the suite. (4) TC-07 ('provider switch does not render stale session A usage') is tautological: it drives two distinct providers with two distinct fetch payloads, and usageByProvider is keyed by provider, so the assertion passes regardless of any staleness handling -- deleting the staleness transition the test is named for does not make it fail. (5) isCtxActive's bare catch reclassifies every error from ctx.hasUI as staleness, including a genuine fault inside the runner itself, silently disabling the usage bar with no diagnostic trace.
